Can you explain the main options in simple terms?
Here's a simple breakdown of the main spirit types:
Whiskey is made from fermented grains like barley, corn, rye, or wheat, and has deep, bold flavors that can range from smooth and mellow to spicy and intense.
Bourbon is a specific type of whiskey — all bourbon is whiskey, but not all whiskey is bourbon. It must contain at least 51% corn in its recipe, which gives it a sweeter, smoother character. No added flavoring or coloring is allowed.
Rum is distilled from sugarcane or molasses, giving it a sweet, tropical flavor. It has a slightly more complex flavor than vodka but still a smooth finish, making it great for cocktails or sipping on its own.
Tequila is made from the blue agave plant and comes in different styles (Blanco, Reposado, Añejo) depending on aging time.
Vodka is the most neutral spirit with subtle flavor, making it a perfect base for cocktails.
We carry over 20,000 spirits from around the world, including everything from well-known classics to rare, hard-to-find bottles.

Good question! The good news is you don't need much to get started. Here's what helps:
The essentials:
Water — Have plenty on hand to alternate sips and clear your palate. Adding a few drops of water to your whiskey can also soften the alcohol punch and release flavors, especially helpful for beginners.
A proper glass — Ideally a Glencairn glass or small sherry glass, which helps you properly savor the aroma. A tulip-shaped glass concentrates the whiskey aroma toward your nose. In a pinch, a small wine glass works too — just avoid regular tumblers for tasting since they don't let you smell the aromas properly.
How to drink it:
Neat (straight up) is the championed method if you want to truly taste the spirit
On the rocks (over ice) can be refreshing if you're acclimatizing yourself to whiskey, though it does degrade some flavors. Use big ice cubes or spheres — they melt slower and water it down less.
With a splash of water to open up the flavors

How do I use it properly the very first time?
• Just now
Seen • Just now
Great question! Here's how to properly taste whiskey for the first time:
Step 1: The Aroma (Nosing)
Gently bring the glass up to your nose — don't rush this! You don't want to overwhelm your nose. Some people even nose with one nostril first, then both. Take your nose away from the glass after each sniff, trust the first thing you smell, then repeat and other layers will slowly reveal themselves.
Tilt the glass to one side and really get your nose in there. Give it a little swirl and admire the legs as they cascade down the side of the glass.
Step 2: The Taste
Take a small sip and roll the spirit over your tongue and around its sides, then all throughout your mouth. Savor the flavors and start identifying them — are they weak or strong? Herbal? Woody? Fruity? Spicy? At the same time, take note of the mouth-feel, which refers to both the texture and intensity.
Pro tips:
Pour about three-quarters of an ounce — you don't need much
Have water on hand to alternate sips and clear your palate
After a while, give your nose a break with fresh air and water
With Bushmills, you should pick up vanilla, honey, and toasted wood notes. Take your time and enjoy the experience!
